## Result

Research for #601: two independent subagents demonstrated call-site static rejection of ZonedDatetime ordering with ty 0.0.84 against temporary copies of the real package. No production source or dependencies changed.

- ty Intersection/Not plus the existing column value witness preserves ordinary declarations and selected exact field/query result types without assuming Python comparability implies database order safety.
- A conventional restricted-self/Python-ordering protocol independently proves the checker/descriptor bridge, but is not a sound general storage capability policy.
- Parent reproduced the baseline (13 forbidden ordering calls accepted), the restricted acceptance (all 20 expected negative sites diagnosed, positive examples pass), and replayed the retained fixtures from a fresh temp directory.

## Scope limits

This is a narrow feasibility proof, not complete enforcement. Experimental ty-specific API, generic-helper constraints and runtime annotation introspection require further assessment. Some column-comparison/aggregate/derived-query paths remain open, explicitly demonstrated by fixtures. Arbitrary Annotated storage capabilities are not inferred. No backend suites or runtime API implementation.

Report and replay instructions: `research/static_ordering_601/README.md`.

## Validation

- Replayed positive/negative fixture acceptance: passed as described above.
- `uv run ty check`: passed.
- `uv run ruff check .`: passed.
- `uv run ruff format --check .`: passed.

Original experimental `.patch` artifacts retain unified-diff blank context lines; these generate whitespace-check notices when treated as newly added text. They are not production patches to apply as-is. Executable probe builder edits only a fresh temporary copy.
title: Research static rejection of ZonedDatetime ordering with ty (#601)
